clue.text: Leather, fake I say

parts.note: a fake is a sham, a pretence or counterfeit
'My!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'I say!'

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a piece of leather is counterfeit.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamois leather, spelt the way it is pronounced, is a soft cleaning leather.

clue.text: Cosmic light initially alters forms

indicators.note: forms as a verb, making something new out of the letters
the opening letter of the word light

explanation.surface: Starlight at first changes shapes in space.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the stars, so to the heavens or cosmos.

clue.text: Pooped nothing out then?

definitions.meaning: if every item is inside, nothing is outside

explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted is the slang sense; literally everyone inside means none left outside.

clue.text: Assaults exciting — still on police record?

parts.note: mugs means attacks in the street to rob
hot, as in a hot topic

explanation.surface: Thrilling assaults that may land someone with a criminal record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb but is a noun: a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo taken of an arrested suspect for the files is a still kept with the police record.

clue.text: Germany's sound leader in Angela's in 23

indicators.note: one thing set in another, so the pick goes inside the word for power

parts.note: the clue at 23 begins with 'Power', and vigour or power is oomph

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of Angela's

explanation.surface: A German political leader, Angela Merkel, is pictured providing the nation's voice with some power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in 23' sends you to 23-down, whose first word 'Power' gives OOMPH; 'leader in' takes the A of Angela's, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The oom-pah is the rhythmic brass-band thump typical of German beer-hall music.

clue.text: Authorised reference covering talk that's come up

indicators.note: the dictionary goes around the chatter

parts.note: the OED, Oxford English Dictionary, is a reference work

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top, so the word for talk runs backwards

parts.note: yak is chatter

explanation.surface: A sanctioned reference including a conversation that has arisen.
explanation.definitionFit: Approved, given the go-ahead, which is to authorise.

clue.text: Astronomical topic, male boobs

indicators.note: boobs as a verb, blunders, so the letters are botched into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about men's chests being an astronomical topic.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the Earth-centred model of the universe set out by an ancient Greek astronomer.

clue.text: Whiffy — as a goose may be?

definitions.meaning: a goose makes a loud trumpeting call

explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this word for reeking, and a goose's cry is the same word.

clue.text: This hen wouldn't want to be turning her friends out

definitions.text: This hen wouldn't want to be

indicators.note: turning over and around, so the letters of her friends out are reordered

explanation.surface: A hen refusing to betray her friends to the farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken coated in seasoned batter and fried is a dish no hen would choose to become.

clue.text: Good grades Paul was always unable to attain — who would have thought it!

parts.note: well as in 'good, so...' or doing well, a synonym of good

parts.words: grades Paul was always unable to attain
parts.note: the setter, Paul, speaking as 'I', confesses that he never did achieve such grades

explanation.surface: The setter ruefully admits he never got top marks at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as Paul answering 'Good grades?' with a sheepish confession of his own.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of astonishment, equivalent to saying one is amazed by the news.

clue.text: Touring middle of farm, muck encountered — mess about

parts.note: goo is sticky muck or sludge

indicators.note: going round, so the word for encountered encloses the next piece

parts.note: found, as in came upon

indicators.note: the central letters of the word farm

explanation.surface: A trip round a farmyard where someone meets muck and makes a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool around idly is the same as messing about.

clue.text: Secure fifty picnic hampers

indicators.note: a hamper holds things, so the word for picnic contains the numeral

parts.note: something that is no picnic is hard, so a picnic is an easy task, a cinch
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty picnic baskets are being made secure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hampers' looks like the baskets of the picnic but works as a verb meaning holds in.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a deal is to settle or secure it firmly.

clue.text: Mere hint about unusual instrument

indicators.note: about meaning round in a different order, so the letters of mere hint are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slight suggestion concerning an odd musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The theremin is an electronic instrument played without touch, waving the hands near two antennae, which makes it decidedly odd.

clue.text: Growth of intellect in Essex?

parts.note: the brain is the seat of intellect
a tree is a plant growth

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether intellect ever grows in Essex.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is a county east of London, often teased in British humour; the town sits in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town located in that county east of London, so something found there.

clue.text: See 9
Make sense, as might exhibits in gallery collection?

definitions.meaning: to be coherent and consistent, as a story that holds up

definitions.text: as might exhibits in gallery collection?
definitions.meaning: pictures in an exhibition are put up on the walls side by side

explanation.surface: Pictures displayed as a set in a gallery also need to be coherent.
explanation.definitionFit: A coherent argument is said to be consistent; paintings shown as a group are literally put on the wall in one show.

clue.text: See 25
Scent style in rose I gathered

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, the hairstyle within the jumble
gathered as in pulled together loosely, so rose and I are jumbled

parts.note: a do is a hairstyle

explanation.surface: Someone picks roses for their perfume and fancy style.
explanation.definitionFit: To perfume something, giving it a smell, is to scent it.

clue.text: 'Loose women': clue de trop

indicators.note: letters let loose are freed to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A setter's aside that a clue about loose women is out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: De trop, borrowed from French, means too much or not wanted, as an unwanted guest is.

clue.text: Every other one blocked off, set up roads vital for an enormous area of land

indicators.note: alternate letters are removed, leaving the even letters of set up roads vital

explanation.surface: Roadworks shut every second route, though the roads are vital for a large region.
explanation.definitionFit: The combined landmass of Europe and Asia, the largest on Earth.

clue.text: Descent of celestial body, twinkling before dawn

parts.note: in a twinkling means in a moment, a mo
the dawn of something is its beginning, its onset

explanation.surface: The moon sinks, the stars twinkle, just before daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment the moon sinks below the horizon.

clue.text: See 23
See 15
Eagle, for example, hit rocky peak

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An eagle strikes from a craggy summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagles are birds of prey, the class that word names.

clue.text: Might exhibitionist stand naked under this?

definitions.text: Might exhibitionist stand naked under this?

parts.note: might means strength or force
a show-er, one who shows off

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a show-off would stand nude beneath a strong spray.
explanation.definitionFit: A pumped bathroom spray, under which anyone stands unclothed.

clue.text: Dark snake and lady of the night?

parts.note: to snake is to wind, to twist and turn
a made-up feminine for the nocturnal bird, owl plus the female ending -ess

explanation.surface: A dark snake and a prostitute, as in some sleazy thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lady of the night' looks like a prostitute but is a female owl, coined in the style of lioness.
explanation.definitionFit: A room with no windows lets in no light, so it is dark.

clue.text: Affect suddenly with strong push in sustained campaign

indicators.note: one piece sits inside another, the push inside the campaign

parts.note: a war, as in a war on crime
a shove is a forceful push

explanation.surface: A strong push during a long political campaign has a sudden effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling that sweeps over you overwhelms you all at once.

clue.text: Bear in river on purpose

indicators.note: the river comes on, that is after, the purpose

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A bear deliberately placed in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear hardship is to tolerate or withstand it.

clue.text: Bird: 22 out of one's tree?

indicators.note: crazy, so the letters of that answer go wild into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 22-across, the bird of prey clued there

explanation.surface: A bird of prey gone mad, fittingly out of its tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking tropical bird famed for mimicry.
